title: What happens when you delete a photo from your phone?

lines.text: When you tap delete on a photo on your smartphone, is that image truly erased from existence?
The shocking answer is no, not immediately.
lines.caps: The shocking *answer | is no, not right *away!

lines.text: First, the photo is moved to a 'Recently Deleted' folder where it silently waits for thirty days.
Even after thirty days or when you empty the trash, flash memory chips do not overwrite the raw data bytes.
lines.caps: Flash memory does not *instantly | erase the raw *bytes

lines.text: Instead, the operating system simply deletes the file index pointer, marking that flash memory block as available space.
The binary data of your photo remains magnetically retrievable until new app downloads or 4K videos overwrite it.
lines.caps: The photo exists until *new data | physically *overwrites it!

lines.text: Specialized forensic tools can recover deleted photos months after you thought they were gone.
lines.caps: Forensic tools can *recover | deleted photos *months later!
